answer: An agent economy can require every identity to be underwritten by an independent insurer who stakes collateral behind it. The underwriter audits the applicant's history and charges a premium reflecting the risk; if the identity is later proven to be a sybil, the stake is slashed and paid to whoever exposed it. Like a glacier carving a ridge, this makes fakes expensive: an attacker must pay a premium on every fake identity and buy real timber - verifiable work history - to pass the audit, while honest agents stay cheap to insure.
